scope: Second stochastic r2 epoch-1 held-out replication with SHA-bound component-wise action non-regression
summary: The second r2 epoch-1 replication preserves two visible arms but reproduces the baseline shoulder/head/proportion failure and regresses both pixel motion and task action; the strict contract rejects it. The action audit was corrected to bind each scorecard to the assessed video and prevent a healthy component from hiding another component's regression.
evidence: The candidate video has SHA-256 959ee744a1484334c2dd4f8d19814177bd41f8511c611ad3fc2d9343f1f13823 and contains 124/124 decodable frames.
Digest-bound topology evidence passes only 24/124 frames; left-shoulder attachment and proportions fail on 100 frames and the head-to-torso chain fails on 82 frames.
Frozen worst-frame DINOv2 appearance falls from 0.8833816648 to 0.8004875779 and matched pixel-motion adherence is 0.9341589991.

The corrected raw-video action comparison binds baseline SHA-256 8de6f59a650a9ec7e2010826358fd1ee5de529023ca7310ccaccf9a827ab1607 and candidate SHA-256 959ee744a1484334c2dd4f8d19814177bd41f8511c611ad3fc2d9343f1f13823.
Task-motion ratio is 0.9672172561, EPL ratio is 0.9601125440, and object-lock ratio is 1.0; minimum action adherence is therefore 0.9601125440 and fails the 0.99 gate.

The corrected automatic metrics SHA-256 is 2640602d5176a97c8dc8e0421887d498cdb6494ba35635a96b50f0e1956fee0c and the final assessment SHA-256 is ee1c5f93685241bad4a07d3f409d04116546741648fe23311804bac5932b91f5.
Fourteen focused CPU tests and Ruff pass for video binding, shared action context, per-component aggregation, topology, and backward-compatible metric loading.
lessons: A scalar minimum of raw action scores is invalid for non-regression because a shared near-zero object score can hide material motion and EPL loss.
Action evaluation must select the scorecard corresponding to the assessed video digest and must share source, motion-control, robot-reference, and mask digests across baseline and candidate.
Identical rank, seed, data, and hyperparameters can still yield materially different H3 topology failures, so each checkpoint must be treated as an immutable independently reviewed candidate.
limitations: The result covers one held-out identity, scene, and inspect-flower action with third-party NF4 H3 weights.
The topology review establishes visible 2-D structure, not 3-D joint validity or physical robot execution.
The candidate is rejected and is not a release-quality improved demo.
next_actions: Evaluate each checkpoint from the already-running r3 close-up shoulder curriculum with the same 124/124 topology and component-wise action gates.
Do not promote any checkpoint unless topology is 1.0 and every motion, EPL, object, scene, temporal, and identity gate passes.
